docs.title: MechWarrior 4: Mercenaries - Oracle Documentation
docs.text:
This site documents the oracle recompilation: a byte-identical reproduction of MW4Mercs.exe and the six code-bearing game DLLs, produced by transcribing the original machine code into MSVC6 inline assembly.

The target is the PR1 MW4Mercs.exe build identified by the SHA-256 in reference/SHA256.txt; see the build guide. The repository contains the transcribed source, the generated data sections, build/verification tooling, and research notes. It does not contain the original game executables, DLLs, art, audio, or maps. The default build does not need the game binaries.

docs.title: The oracle idea
docs.text:
The target binaries were compiled with Microsoft Visual C++ 6.0. To reproduce them byte-for-byte, each function is transcribed from its original machine code into a __declspec(naked) MSVC6 inline-assembly function. The compiler emits the transcribed instructions directly; no C++ code generation is involved.

Every func_<VA>.c source is therefore both:

  • a readable, annotated record of the function's instructions and behavior, and
  • an input to a build that must reproduce the reference bytes exactly.

The result is an oracle: a source tree that compiles to the canonical binary. It is not an attempt to recover the original C++ source.

docs.title: Source layout
docs.text:
Sources are organized by binary target and PE section, not by subsystem:

src/
  mw4mercs/
    text/        func_<VA>.c + in-.text data_<VA>.c
    rdata/       data_0x*.c section runs
    data/        data_0x*.c section runs
    rsrc/        data_0x*.c section runs
    txt2/        SafeDisc .txt2 leftover
    artifacts/   committed PE build artifacts + CSV metadata
  blade/         text/ rdata/ data/ artifacts/
  gundll/        text/ rdata/ data/ artifacts/
  language/      text/ rdata/ data/ artifacts/
  missionlang_mercs/  text/ rdata/ data/ artifacts/
  mw4stats/      text/ rdata/ data/ artifacts/
  zloglib/       text/ rdata/ data/ artifacts/

Filenames are canonical: func_<8-hex-va>.c and data_<8-hex-va>.c. Semantics live in the file header and inline comments, never in the filename. The per-binary subsystem indexes under docs/va_index/ provide the semantic map.

Non-.text sections (.rdata, .data, .rsrc, .txt2) are byte-exact data runs. The generated data_0x*.c sources are committed, so the default build does not need the reference. nmake data remains the optional regeneration path; see BUILD.md.

docs.title: Building an image
docs.text:
The default EXE build has three stages:

  1. Compile .text sources — all src/mw4mercs/text/*.c are compiled with the pinned MSVC6 flags into build/obj/.
  2. Compile data sources — the committed src/mw4mercs/{rdata,data,rsrc,txt2}/data_0x*.c runs are compiled into build/obj/data/.
  3. Assemble — exe_image_assemble.py places every object at its reference RVA, resolves relocation sites, fills pads from the committed artifact, composes the sections, and writes build/MW4Mercs.exe. --diff compares the result to the reference when it is present.

The PE header, inter-function pad bytes, and residual extern table are committed artifacts. exe_image_assemble.py --init is the optional regeneration path that rebuilds them from a reference EXE.

Module DLLs use the same model with data_assemble.py and image_assemble.py; their data sources and .bin artifacts are committed. gundll's in-scope VA list is provided at reference/in_scope/gundll.txt for its coverage report.

docs.title: Relocation resolution
docs.text:
An unlinked object's relocation slots contain placeholder values. The assembler resolves each slot from the symbol name:

  1. Address-embedded names (FUN_00401000, g_0076B000, ...).
  2. The committed src/<target>/artifacts/extern_addrs.csv table for residual symbols whose names carry no address.
  3. The import map parsed from the assembled .rdata for imported functions.

The committed extern table is authoritative. The source-comment fallback is legacy and must never drive the build; the assembler hard-errors if a symbol would resolve that way.

docs.title: Verification model
docs.text:
There are four levels of checking:

  • Hash gate — compares the built image to the canonical SHA-256; this is the reference-free acceptance check.
  • Full-image byte diff — composes the complete binary and compares it to a reference binary when one is present. It catches ordering, padding, alignment, relocation, and section-composition errors.
  • Masked per-function diff — compares one compiled object against the reference function, masking 4-byte relocation sites.
  • No-mask per-function check — places the object at its VA, resolves every relocation, and compares every byte.

The hash gate is the default gate. The byte-level checks are optional diagnostics that require the reference binaries.

docs.title: What is intentionally out of scope
docs.text:
• The .txt2 SafeDisc leftover (preserved only as generated bytes for layout).
  • DRM/SafeDisc components and the bundled DRM DLLs.
  • CRT and middleware code that is not game logic.
  • The four editor/config tools shipped with the game (documented under docs/editor_tools/, not oracle targets).
  • ScriptStrings_MERCS.dll (resource-only, no code).

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Windows 10 or 11. The build tools are 32-bit and run on 64-bit Windows.
  • Microsoft Visual C++ 6.0 with SP6: cl.exe 12.00.8804, link.exe 6.00.8447, and the matching nmake.exe. SP6 matters; earlier VC6 builds do not produce the oracle's instruction encoding.
  • DirectX 8.1 SDK headers and libraries.
  • Python 3.8+ on PATH.

The build uses nmake. Run commands from a cmd.exe prompt in the repository root.

docs.title: Provenance
docs.text:
The oracle reproduces the official MechWarrior 4: Mercenaries Point Release 1 (PR1) build:

Item Value Release Point Release 1 (PR1), the final official point release EXE file version 50.07.01.2105 EXE size 3,915,776 bytes EXE SHA-256 deb0cb7f97e26c9db850d768900bdfb7648db7d10a090e7cdf6cecdc7686134f

This is provenance, not a build prerequisite. The reference-derived non-.text data sources and the committed .bin artifacts are part of the repository, so the default build does not need the original EXE or DLLs. The hashes remain in reference/SHA256.txt for optional regeneration and verification.

The baseline is the original PR1 engine, not a community build such as MekTek 3.1. See game versioning for how the EXE uses 50.07.01.2105 in multiplayer and saved data.

docs.title: 1. Configure the environment
docs.text:
call tools\env.bat

The script derives MW4_ROOT from its own location and sets PATH, INCLUDE, and LIB for VC6. Override the install locations if needed:

set VC98=C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\VC98
set DXSDK=C:\dx81full\DXF\DXSDK
call tools\env.bat

Check the compiler:

cl

docs.title: 2. Reference binaries (optional)
docs.text:
The default build does not read the reference binaries. The repository contains the generated non-.text data sources and the reference-derived .bin artifacts, so you can build without owning or supplying the game.

The reference binaries are needed only for these optional operations:

  • nmake data / nmake module-data - regenerate data sources from a reference.
  • nmake init / nmake dll-init - regenerate metadata artifacts.
  • nmake exe / nmake dll - run the final byte diff (skipped if the reference file is absent).
  • nmake diff / nmake nomask - per-function comparison.

If you want those checks, copy your own files into reference/ and verify them against reference/SHA256.txt (for example with certutil -hashfile reference\MW4Mercs.exe SHA256). Reference binaries remain ignored by git.

docs.title: 3. Build the EXE oracle
docs.text:
nmake objs
nmake data-objs
nmake exe

Or:

nmake all

What each step does:

Step Output nmake objs build\obj\*.obj from every src\mw4mercs\text\*.c nmake data-objs build\obj\data\*.obj from the committed src\mw4mercs\{rdata,data,rsrc,txt2}\data_0x*.c nmake exe build\MW4Mercs.exe; byte diff only if reference\MW4Mercs.exe is present

nmake data and nmake init are the optional regeneration path. They read the reference to rebuild the committed data sources/artifacts; you do not need them for a normal build.

docs.title: 4. Build a module oracle
docs.text:
nmake dll-all MOD=gundll

Valid module keys:

blade  gundll  language  missionlang  mw4stats  zloglib

The steps are:

nmake module-objs MOD=gundll
nmake module-data-objs MOD=gundll
nmake dll MOD=gundll

nmake dll assembles build\modules\<key>\dll\<name>.dll and byte-diffs it when the corresponding reference DLL is present. The module's header.bin, rsrc.bin, reloc.bin, text_pads.bin, trailer.bin, and extern_addrs.csv are committed under src\<target>\artifacts\. nmake dll-init is the optional path that regenerates them from a reference DLL.

docs.title: 5. Verify
docs.text:
nmake verify

Expected hashes are in reference/SHA256.txt. The command checks the EXE and all six built DLLs, so build every module first if you want a full pass.

docs.title: Per-function workflow (optional)
docs.text:
These checks compare one source file against a reference binary, so they need the corresponding file under reference/:

nmake one SRC=src\mw4mercs\text\func_00401000.c
nmake diff FUNC=0x00401000 OBJNAME=build\obj\func_00401000.obj
nmake nomask FUNC=0x00401000 OBJNAME=build\obj\func_00401000.obj

The masked diff ignores relocation slots. The no-mask check resolves them from the committed table and compares every byte.

docs.title: Windows 11 notes
docs.text:
The compiler and linker are 32-bit, so they run on 64-bit Windows 11. The installers are the problem: Visual Studio 6.0 and the DirectX 8.1 SDK predate 64-bit Windows and may refuse to run or register components.

Visual C++ 6.0 installation fails. The original VS6 installer predates 64-bit Windows and often fails on Windows 11. Try setup.exe in Windows XP (SP3) compatibility mode as administrator first. If it still fails:

  • Install VC6 with SP6 in a 32-bit Windows VM and share the repository into the VM.
  • Use a pre-extracted or portable VC98 tree and point VC98 at it.
  • Copy an existing VC98 installation from a 32-bit machine.

The build only needs the VC98 Bin, Include, and Lib directories; a full IDE installation is not required. Short paths without spaces are safest:

set VC98=C:\VC98
set DXSDK=C:\dx81full\DXF\DXSDK
call tools\env.bat

The DirectX 8.1 SDK installer fails. The old installer may refuse to run. Extract or copy the SDK files and point DXSDK at the directory containing Include and Lib. The build does not need the SDK installer to run.

cl or nmake is the wrong version. A modern Visual Studio installation may be earlier on PATH. Run tools\env.bat in the same cmd.exe session and check cl reports 12.00.8804. Do not use nmake from Visual Studio 2022.

PowerShell environment. tools\env.bat is a batch file. Run it from cmd.exe; invoking a .bat from PowerShell runs it in a child process, so the environment does not persist.

The game will not start. For multiplayer, enable the legacy DirectPlay component in Windows Features. If the game or an old tool still fails, try Windows XP (SP3) compatibility mode and "Run as administrator". For display scaling problems, use the shortcut's compatibility settings and set "Override high DPI scaling behavior" to "Application".

Old binaries are quarantined. Antivirus and SmartScreen may flag VC6 tools, the SafeDisc-era game files, or the reference executable. Add a local exclusion for the build and game directories if you trust the files; do not disable real-time protection globally.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
cl not found or wrong version — tools\env.bat did not find VC6. Set VC98 explicitly and rerun it.

Cannot open include file: 'mw4/archive.h' — run from the repository root so /Iinclude resolves, or use tools\compile_one.bat.

missing committed artifacts / empty extern table — run nmake objs before nmake init. init learns symbols from the compiled objects.

Data-section mismatch — your reference binary does not match the expected hash. Verify reference/SHA256.txt.

Module data mismatch — make sure the matching DLL in reference/ is the canonical one; each module is diffed against its own binary.

Build is slow — the first EXE build compiles ~13,800 translation units. Subsequent builds are incremental. build_text_objs.py skips objects that are newer than their sources.

nmake dll says missing artifacts — the committed artifact is missing; restore it from the repository, or run nmake dll-init MOD=... with a reference DLL.

docs.title: Clean
docs.text:
nmake clean

This removes build/ but leaves the committed data sources and artifacts under src/ in place.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Is this the original source code? No. It is a disassembly transcription: every function is __declspec(naked) MSVC6 inline assembly that recompiles to the original bytes. It is not a source reconstruction.

Why not write clean C++? Byte identity is the acceptance criterion. Reconstructed C++ would compile to different bytes, so the oracle transcribes the original machine code instead.

Does this repository include the game or its assets? No original executables, DLLs, art, audio, or maps are included. The repository does include transcribed code and reference-derived data sections, so the default build is self-contained.

Do I need to supply the game EXE or DLLs? No. The generated non-.text data sources and the reference-derived .bin artifacts are committed. You can build and verify the oracle without owning the game. The reference binaries are optional and are needed only to regenerate data/artifacts or to run byte diffs. See the build guide.

Why are the data sections included now? The earlier layout regenerated them from a user-supplied reference. To make the repository buildable as-is, the byte-exact data sources and artifacts are now committed. nmake data and nmake init remain available as the optional "how they were created" regeneration path.

Which game version was used as the baseline? The official Microsoft MechWarrior 4: Mercenaries Point Release 1 (PR1) build, file version 50.07.01.2105, EXE SHA-256 deb0cb7f97e26c9db850d768900bdfb7648db7d10a090e7cdf6cecdc7686134f. This is provenance; you do not need the file to build. Community builds such as MekTek 3.1 are different product builds and are not the baseline.

Can I build a playable EXE? The build produces a byte-identical MW4Mercs.exe from the committed sources and artifacts. You can deploy it with nmake deploy if your install is in the expected location.

Why MSVC6? The target binaries were built with MSVC6. The inline-assembly encoding and the final image layout depend on that toolchain.

Why are some functions missing? A few EXE IAT jump thunks and the .txt2 SafeDisc leftover are out of scope. They are listed in src/mw4mercs/artifacts/extra_functions.csv.

How do I know the build is correct? nmake verify checks the built images against the canonical SHA-256 hashes without needing the reference. nmake exe, nmake dll-all MOD=..., and the per-function checks additionally compare bytes when the reference is present. See docs/VERIFICATION.md.

Can I contribute code? No. The oracle is frozen. Documentation corrections are welcome; see CONTRIBUTING.md.

Does the build need an external analysis database? No. The build uses the committed sources, the committed function inventories in reference/functions/, and the committed data/artifacts. The reference binaries are optional.

docs.title: Game versioning in the reference (MW4Mercs.exe)
docs.text: How the reference build identifies its version and how that identity is used to keep multiplayer clients on the same version. All addresses are reference VAs; function names are the oracle's func_<VA> names. This is reference (oracle) RE.

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text:
• One version value, stored in two hardcoded copies: "50.07.01.2105" (.rdata 0x0076CB3C, loaded at startup into g_game_version 0x00858924, and 0x00773040, read by the join handshake and saved-data paths). This is the official Point Release 1 (PR1) build.
  • Hosts advertise it as the DirectPlay session attribute GameVersion (and inside the session config blob as the \v directive).
  • The server browser compares each enumerated session's GameVersion against the local one with whole-string lexicographic compares (_stricmp in the filter, _mbscmp in the sort — no numeric parsing; older = string less than local, newer = greater). Three UI toggles (curveroff / newveroff / oldveroff) and a 6-mode versionsort control filter and order the list; the UI shows the selected server's version as ReferenceVersion next to LocalGameVersion.
  • The Zone matchmaking layer has its own protocol-version gate; its failure string is "Incompatible Protocol version mismatch." (0x007A04DC, ZoneTech error 0xC1120C05).
  • There is an in-game join handshake (net event 0x0A, FUN_0053F210, §7): the joiner sends a packed 64-bit version code (derived from "50.07.01.2105") and an 8-byte content checksum; the receiver compares both against its own computation and answers 0x0B (reject + status) or 0x0C (accept + checksum echo the joiner re-verifies in FUN_0053F9B0). Mismatches log Player_Reject\t%d\t%d (0x0077B730) with status 4 (content), 5 (version), 6 (banned IP) or 8 (duplicate player GUID). The content checksum covers the code bytes of the 15 resource-loader functions plus one mission archive entry (§8).
  • The connect path's DirectPlay application GUID (0x007A2E30 = {36E95EE0-8577-11CF-960C-0080C7534E82}) is game identity only, identical across builds. The advertisement + browser filter/sort is advisory; the join handshake is the actual same-build gate.
  • The handshake and the variant self-digest are the game's two integrity checks; §10 describes what each one covers, and §11 lists the observed limitations.

docs.title: 1. The version value
docs.text:
Item Address Notes Build version string 0x0076CB3C "50.07.01.2105" Local version global 0x00858924 char* in BSS, zero-initialized Option/config init FUN_00407BE0 0x00407BE0: sets g_858924 = 0x76CB3C Log/registry init FUN_00737020 0x00737020: calls FUN_00407BE0, then a fallback

FUN_00737020 (called from the startup/log init FUN_00709120 and FUN_007374B0) calls the big option-init FUN_00407BE0, which assigns g_game_version = "50.07.01.2105". Only if that pointer were still null/empty would FUN_00737020 build a date-derived fallback wsprintfA(0x008AA390, "00.00.%02d.%02d00", month, day) (format 0x007A6958) and point g_858924 at it — dead in the normal path.

The version string doubles as a per-version registry value name: the registry key is "Software\Microsoft\Microsoft Games\%s" (format 0x007A6918) and FUN_007086D0 / FUN_00708880 read/write a value named by g_858924 (window size, perf counter, exe date). So each build keeps its own settings.

docs.title: 1.1 The four fields (and the two hardcoded copies)
docs.text:
The string is four .-separated decimal fields of 2+2+2+4 digits (50 07 01 2105). Nothing in the game assigns meaning to them individually — the fallback format "00.00.%02d.%02d00" (month in field 3, day×100 in field 4) is the only hint at the intended shape, and the shipped family shows the convention:

Binary Version Note MW4Mercs.exe 50.07.01.2105 this target MW4Ed2.exe 50.06.10.0801 mission editor (older) autoconfig_MERCS.exe 50.06.09.3002 graphics config tool

(50 = MW4 family, field 2 = title/generation, field 3 = minor series, field 4 = build number; see docs/editor_tools/ for the tool versions.)

There are two hardcoded copies, both read-only literals, and they are read by different subsystems:

Copy Address Consumers g_858924 target 0x0076CB3C UI (LocalGameVersion), browser filter/sort, session advertisement, gundll wide conversion, registry key, log init DAT_00773040 0x00773040 join handshake version code (FUN_00535F30), GameSpy gamever (FUN_004D8A80, FUN_004FF490), log header (FUN_00563800), saved-game version compare (FUN_00616830), stats (FUN_00564AA0, FUN_00565E00), mission/save data (FUN_00614A80, FUN_00615100, FUN_00615FF0, FUN_0061A510)

A third copy is the unreferenced what-string "@(#) Microsoft MechWarrior IV: Mercenaries Build 50.07.01.2105" (0x007B4640, no pointers into it). Both live copies have ~2 bytes of zero-padding slack before the next literal (usable string length ≈ 14 chars + NUL), so an in-place overwrite is possible; changing only one of them makes the advertised version and the join version code disagree.

docs.title: Where the player sees it
docs.text:
The multiplayer UI (bound in FUN_00404D60 / FUN_00404AC5) has three version fields:

UI field name Name string Backing global Meaning GameVersion 0x0076C218 0x007B7C70 version of the session currently selected/received (FUN_00401E50 GetGameData) ReferenceVersion 0x0076C260 0x007B7E44 version of the selected server, filled on demand LocalGameVersion 0x0076C274 0x00858924 this client's own version

ReferenceVersion is filled by the UI event GetReferenceVersion (0x0076C4E0); its handler at 0x004010B0 (inside func_00401006.c) takes the browser's current selection (FUN_006F6350, which returns the selected entry or NULL), reads its GameVersion attribute (FUN_006F5B80) and strncpys it (0xFF bytes) into 0x007B7E44. It is informational — the player compares the two strings on the server-info panel.

The version also goes out in:

  • the log header (Game_Version block at 0x0077EA3x, writer FUN_00563800 — game name/version/author/server info), and
  • the gundll (GunDll) interface init (FUN_006FCF00 / FUN_00701030 convert g_858924 to wide and pass it to the gundll vtable at 0x008589A4).

docs.title: 2. How it is advertised (host side)
docs.text:
The session config is a backslash-directive blob parsed by FUN_00705D80 (0x00705D80):

\g<name>   -> session+0x1878   (game name)
\m<map>    -> session+0x1834   (map type)
\v<ver>    -> session+0x18B8   (GAME VERSION)
\a / \h / \r -> session+0x18F8 / +0x1938 / +0x1978 (UnlimitedAmmo / NoHeat / NoRespawn)
\p<xy>     -> session+0xC34 + idx*0x40  (per-player name, count at +0x1874)
\c<xy>     -> session+0x1234 + idx*0x40 (per-player clan)

Two registration paths publish the DirectPlay session attributes:

  • FUN_00705FE0 (0x00705FE0, "game creation / server info registration") copies the lobby record's config blob (lobby+0x30, 3000 bytes) into session+0x7C, parses it with FUN_00705D80, then sets GameVersion = session+0x18B8 — i.e. the advertised version is whatever the host's \v directive says. It also sets Mod Name, Product Name, IpAddr, ServerPort, GName, player/bot counts, MaxPlayers, MapType, PasswordProtected, Instance, Handle, Flags, Protocol, GameType, Update Time, ExpectRefresh="false", UnlimitedAmmo, NoHeat, NoRespawn, and one entry per player. FUN_00705F9C is the sibling variant of the same routine.
  • FUN_007008E0 (0x007008E0, IGunHost::AddPlayer) sets GameVersion = g_858924 directly (wide), alongside MaxPlayers, PasswordProtected (L"No"/L"Yes"), Instance, MapType ("-"), Flags, GameType ("0").

Instance is the game-instance GUID (a 16-byte game ID formatted with "{%08X-%04X-%04X-%02X%02X-%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X}", 0x007A1120), not a version derivative. GameVersion is the only build-version field on the wire (a plain string).

docs.title: 3. Client-side matching (server browser)
docs.text: Session attributes are read with FUN_006F5B80(obj, "GameVersion") and compared as whole strings — _stricmp (0x0076B2AC, case-insensitive) in the filter, _mbscmp (0x0076B300, case-sensitive) in the sort. There is no numeric/semantic version parsing anywhere: "older" means the entry's version string is lexicographically less than the local g_858924 string, "newer" means greater (argument order in the calls is (entry, local)). That works only because the shipped string uses fixed-width zero-padded fields (50.07.01.2105); an unpadded field breaks the order ("50.7.x" > "50.10.x" lexicographically, although 50.7 < 50.10 numerically), and the filter (_stricmp) and sort (_mbscmp) even disagree on case.

docs.title: 3.1 The filter callback
docs.text:
FUN_006F6EB0 (0x006F6EB0, a method of the filter object vtable at 0x0079FD24) implements three version predicates against g_858924, enabled by bytes of the filter object:

Filter byte Predicate (_stricmp(entry, local), entry = session GameVersion) +0x40 (curveroff) equal (== 0) +0x41 (newveroff) entry newer (entry > local, > 0) +0x42 (oldveroff) entry older (entry < local, < 0)

(The UI names agree: newveroff = hide newer, oldveroff = hide older.)

The callback is invoked with a mode (1–4) that encodes the ZoneTech filter engine's AND/OR polarity: mode 1 rejects when the predicate holds, mode 2 accepts when it fails, mode 3 accepts when it holds, mode 4 rejects when it fails; unset bytes simply fall through. A missing GameVersion attribute is treated as predicate-false. The remaining filter bytes cover the non-version filters (ping/gametype/players/clan/available/active).

docs.title: 3.2 The UI filter parameters
docs.text:
FUN_00402660 (0x00402660, SetFilterParam) / FUN_004024B2 (0x004024B2, GetFilterParam) map UI script parameter names to those globals:

Parameter String Global Filter byte curveroff 0x0076B890 0x007B7C60 +0x40 (equal) newveroff 0x0076B878 0x007B7C61 +0x41 (entry newer) oldveroff 0x0076B884 0x007B7C62 +0x42 (entry older) versionsort 0x0076B86C 0x007B7C64 (1–6) sort mode

All default to 0 (no version filtering, no version sort). A bad versionsort value asserts with "Invalid version sorting filter setting '%s'. Should be a number between 1 and 6." (0x0076B94C).

FUN_004022E0 (0x004022E0, ApplyFilters) pushes the three bytes onto the filter object through the trivial setters FUN_006F73B0 / FUN_006F73D0 / FUN_006F73F0 (+0x40/+0x41/+0x42) and the sort mode through FUN_006F79E0.

docs.title: 3.3 The version sort
docs.text:
• FUN_00401140 (0x00401140, the SortGameList UI callback) dispatches on the sort-key name; when the key is "GameVersion" (0x0079FA48) it clamps g_007B7C64 to 0–6 and passes it to FUN_006F7BF0.
  • FUN_006F7BF0 (0x006F7BF0) partitions the list into three groups by _mbscmp(entry_version, g_858924) (case-sensitive): entry < local → older, entry == local → same, entry > local → newer — the same lexicographic comparison as the filter, in the opposite call order and case-sensitively. The mode (1–6) then selects the resulting order/grouping of those three groups; mode 0 leaves the list unsorted by version.
  • FUN_006F7B10 (0x006F7B10) is the attribute-change callback: when an entry's GameVersion (or Flags) attribute arrives/updates, it re-runs the FUN_006F7BF0 reorder.

docs.title: 3.4 List ingestion gate
docs.text: Before an entry is even added to the list, FUN_006FFC90 (0x006FFC90), FUN_006FEAB0 (0x006FEAB0) and FUN_006FF640 (0x006FF640) require the entry's Protocol attribute (0x0079FAD4) to equal "0" (0x0079FB30) and its ExpectRefresh attribute (0x0079FAFC) to equal "false". The Protocol attribute is the lobby/browser protocol marker (set from session+0x78 in FUN_00705F9C), not the build version.

docs.title: 4. The lobby (ZoneTech) protocol gate
docs.text:
The matchmaking layer's error-code→string map is FUN_006FCB40 (0x006FCB40). Its ZoneTech error family 0xC1120xxx includes:

  • 0xC1120C05 → "Incompatible Protocol version mismatch." (0x007A04DC)

That is the hard "your client's protocol/version does not match the lobby" rejection — the closest thing to a version gate in the matchmaking path. The rest of the family (0x007A03E8–0x007A0B8C) covers session/GUID/lobby errors such as "The requested component version in not available." (0x007A0B8C) and "Client is disconnected from the server." (0x007A0424).

docs.title: 5. What is and is not version-gated
docs.text:
• The connect path FUN_00703E60 (0x00703E60) verifies the DirectPlay application GUID at 0x007A2E30 = {36E95EE0-8577-11CF-960C-0080C7534E82} and rejects a mismatch. This identifies the game (MW4 Mercs) and is the same for every build, so it does not separate versions.
  • The advertised GameVersion attribute is not what the join handshake checks. The handshake's version code is computed from the second hardcoded copy DAT_00773040 (§1.1), not from the advertised string nor from g_858924; so a host can advertise an arbitrary GameVersion yet the in-session check still validates the real build (and vice versa).
  • The browser filter/sort is advisory. A client can reach a session whose advertised version differs (join directly, or disable the browser version filters); the lobby protocol check and the join handshake (§7) are the enforcement, and the UI deliberately surfaces both versions (ReferenceVersion vs LocalGameVersion) so the player can decide.
  • What is not gated at all: content outside the 15 hashed loader functions and the mission entry, the peer's actual variant files (only a local self-digest, §9), the peer's identity/IP fields (self-reported), and anything after join (no runtime re-validation, §10).

docs.title: 6. Related version checks (not multiplayer)
docs.text:
For contrast, the binary has many other version checks that are unrelated to client compatibility:

  • Data-format magic+version asserts for MLR/ERF/OBB/GFX/GAF assets — e.g. MLR "MLR#" + version 0x12 (FUN_00421E60 / FUN_00421EC0), ERF (FUN_004AF200), OBB (FUN_004FEC10), with strings like "Application must be rebuilt to use this version of MLR data" (0x0076DD24).
  • Saved-game version (FUN_00616830, message "You are loading a game saved by a newer game version. The saved game might not work correctly.", 0x0078C310) — single player.
  • Diagnostics: GetDLLVersions (0x007A4750) reads file versions via VERSION.dll (GetFileVersionInfoA, 0x007B1318); "Executable version" / "DirectX version" / "GameOS build version" report block (0x007A4A59+).
  • gundll/gun-auth receives the version string at interface init (FUN_006FCF00 / FUN_00701030).
  • DRM/anti-tamper (not multiplayer): FUN_0052A460 is the SafeDisc CD check (CdaSys*, "ScsHD.csa", anti-tamper verification); FUN_0052AAB0 calls the registry/date checks FUN_00536060 / FUN_00536190 ("Date/time validation"); FUN_005FCC80 is a local XOR-checksum/flag check. These are copy-protection/clock-tamper tripwires, unrelated to client compatibility.

docs.title: 7. Join-time validation — net event 0x0A (FUN_0053F210)
docs.text: This is the actual same-build/content gate, and it happens in-session (after the DirectPlay connect). It corrects an earlier reading of this doc: there is a join-time build check.

docs.title: 7.1 The message path
docs.text:
The in-game net dispatcher FUN_00546C60 (0x00546C60) switches on an event id (jump table 0x00547074, index = eventId - 0x0A). The relevant events:

Event Handler Role 0x0A FUN_0053F210 player join/registration message — validate + accept/reject 0x0B FUN_0053F910 join reject reply — sets local session state (this+0x3514 = 2/3/4/5) 0x0C FUN_0053F9B0 join accept reply — joiner re-verifies the echoed checksum; mismatch sets state 3

Flow:

  1. The joiner's sender FUN_0053FA70 (0x0053FA70) builds the 0x0A payload (content checksum via FUN_004D2AB0 + FUN_0062DDC0 at 0x53FAC2 / 0x53FAEE, version code via the FUN_00535F30 family at 0x53FB0C, plus the player record), calls FUN_0053F210 on its own copy (loopback, 0x540021), then transmits.
  2. Every receiving peer runs FUN_0053F210, which recomputes the local reference values into DAT_007DDD50/54 (content checksum), DAT_007DDD58/5C (FUN_00535B40 = 0,0 — reserved), DAT_007DDD60/64 (version code) and sets DAT_007DDD48 = 1 (join-validation-in-progress).
  3. The result goes back as 0x0B (reject) with a 4-byte status, or 0x0C (accept) with an 8-byte re-derived checksum pair; FUN_0053F9B0 recomputes the pair locally and aborts the session (state 3) on mismatch, so the check is mutual.

docs.title: 7.2 The 0x0A payload as read by FUN_0053F210
docs.text:
# Field Size Destination / check 1 content checksum 8 vs DAT_007DDD50/54 → status 4 2 version code 8 vs DAT_007DDD60/64 → status 5 3 flag bytes 3×1 scratch (one becomes slot +0x353F on accept) 4 name length + string 4 + n player slot +0x358C 5 dword 4 slot +0x3590 6 flag1 1 slot +0x355D → triggers GUID1 search 7 flag2 1 slot +0x355E → triggers GUID2 search 8 GUID1 8 slot +0x3594 9 GUID2 8 slot +0x359C 10 data16 16 sender's index word in dword 0 (seed for the accept echo) 11 val5 4 ban-list third key 12 data16b 16 ban-list IP key 13 content checksum again 8 re-checked vs DAT_007DDD50/54 → status 4

Then:

  • GUID searches (only when flag1/flag2 are set): scan the 0x2038-stride player table for a slot with the same GUID1/GUID2 (skipping the joining player's own slot, and slot 1 when a global flag is set); a match sets status 8.
  • Ban check FUN_005450B0 (skipped for the local player index): the 16-byte data16/data16b (IP address words) and val5 are looked up in the three lists at this+0x239D54/58/5C (counts) / +0x239D60/64/68 (data); found → status 6.
  • The status is logged via FUN_00563550 with "Player_Reject\t%d\t%d" (0x0077B730) → FUN_00563C80, and returned as message 0x0B.
  • On accept (status == 0) the slot fields +0x35B4, +0x35B8, +0x353F, +0x35DC (16 bytes), +0x35EC, +0x5558 (16 bytes) are filled, the MOTD chunks at +0x309C are re-broadcast (this vtable slot +0x30), and FUN_00536DF0 / FUN_00543EC0 / FUN_00543BC0 run for non-self players.

docs.title: 7.3 The ban lists
docs.text: FUN_00544B60 (0x00544B60) rebuilds the three lists from the game config (ban.txt): keys ban (0x0077B7B4), ngban (0x0077B7B8), ispban (0x0077B7C8), values parsed with "%d.%d.%d.%d" (0x0077B744) into 16-byte entries (first two lists) / 4-byte entries (third list), initialized from the all-zero 16-byte constant 0x007AFAF0. The lists are (re)built by FUN_00544B60 (called from FUN_00536840 / FUN_005449F0, i.e. when the config/MOTD side reloads) and torn down by FUN_0052FA70.

docs.title: 8. The content checksum — what the peers must match
docs.text:
DAT_007DDD50/54 = FUN_004D2AB0(entry) ^ FUN_0062DDC0(entry), where entry = [game_object + 0x1804] (the mission/archive entry index).

Part Function Hash input Output mission entry FUN_004D2AB0 → FUN_00414A70 MD5 stream: 4-byte entry index + the archive entry's bytes digest[0] ^ digest[8] (8 bits, edx = 0) loader code FUN_0062DDC0 MD5 stream: code bytes of the 15 resource loaders (addresses 0x007B55F8[i], sizes 0x007F2CE0[i]) + 4-byte entry index d0^d1, d2^d3 (64 bits)

The 15 hashed loader regions (sizes computed by FUN_0062D5AB / FUN_0062D67B into 0x007F2CE0..0x007F2D18; addresses from the pointer table 0x007B55F8):

# Address Size # Address Size 0 0x0070E380 0x0B30 8 0x005ECBC0 0x1C50 1 0x004E5FD0 0x20B0 9 0x005ABD30 0x10D0 2 0x004C8E00 0x0160 10 0x005A61D0 0x0780 3 0x006212E0 0x3490 11 0x005EF590 0x03D0 4 0x005B6C20 0x0A90 12 0x0069D490 0x1410 5 0x00548F60 0x12820 13 0x00637F60 0x2DF0 6 0x005F2B00 0x4150 14 0x0062D750 0x06E0 7 0x00581480 0x0FA60

(Entry 14 is the region that contains the checksum helpers themselves, FUN_0062DCD0…FUN_0062DE30.)

DAT_007DDD58/5C = FUN_00535B40 (0x00535B40, xor eax,eax; xor edx,edx; ret) = 0,0 — a reserved/disabled third checksum slot.

The version code (DAT_007DDD60/64) is FUN_00535F30 (0x00535F30): it tokenizes g_858924 on '.', atois the components c0..c3 and packs (((c0*100 + c1)*100 + c2)*10000 + c3) as a 64-bit value (through the __allmul-style FUN_0075DC60). For "50.07.01.2105" that is 5007012105.

Notes:

  • Both hashes are unkeyed MD5 over public data — the only "secret" is the algorithm, which ships in the binary.
  • The mission-entry contribution is 8 bits; the loader-code part is 64 bits.
  • The accept path re-derives the checksum with the peer's entry index (data16[0] ^ 0) and echoes the pair in 0x0C; FUN_0053F9B0 recomputes and compares, so the check is mutual.
  • FUN_0053F210 itself computes the pair twice (top of function and again on accept); FUN_004D2AB0/FUN_0062DDC0 are also called by the sender FUN_0053FA70 and by the joiner's verifier FUN_0053F9B0.

docs.title: 9. Variant (mech) file integrity and loadout validation
9.1 The variant self-digest
docs.text:
When a player-creation message is processed (FUN_00534200 / FUN_00533C30), the receiver:

  1. reads the variant name from the message,
  2. loads Resource\VariantsMercs\<name>.mw4 from its own local database (path format 0x0077B368, fetch FUN_004D2E00; mech resource id via FUN_004D2CB0),
  3. reads the 16-byte digest stored inside the resource (FUN_0041E720, size 0x10),
  4. recomputes MD5(0xA1252388 + resource data) (FUN_0070E390 / E3C0 / E460) — the same salted digest the variant loader FUN_0060C12D (0x0060C12D) computes and appends (FUN_0041F030) when building the resource,
  5. repe cmpsds the two digests; mismatch sets the per-player flag +0x357C = 1 (and +0x3578 holds the loaded mech resource pointer).

Consequences of the flag (both act on the local player's own slot — the mechanism is self-enforcement, not peer enforcement):

  • FUN_005330C0 aborts the local player's mission entry (state +0x3534 → 0, cleanup).
  • FUN_005405B5 pushes event code 1 into the player-event queue at +0x204D2C (count +0x205524); the queue is consumed through the accessor helpers in FUN_00513B60.

Scope: this is a local self-consistency check of the receiver's own copy of the named variant — it catches hand-edited files whose stored digest was not updated. It does not compare the sender's file against the receiver's (the name is the only variant data on the wire), so two clients with different VariantsMercs files still pass and simulate different mechs.

docs.title: 9.2 Loadout legality
docs.text: FUN_005FEEB0 → FUN_00601EF0 validates weapon/armor slot counts against the chassis (mount groups, 0x429 mech-type gate), and FUN_00676EA0 validates the GameData distributions (ArmDistributive / LegDistributive / SideFrontDistributive / CenterFrontDistributive / CenterRearDistributive in 0..1.0, PointsPerFerroTon / PointsPerReflectiveTon / PointsPerReactiveTon > 0). These run on the local copy only; they bound what a legal mech is but are not cross-checked with peers.

docs.title: 10. Trust model — what actually happens to a modded client
docs.text:
Scenario Result Different binary build / patched loader code / different mission entry join rejected, status 4, Player_Reject Different hardcoded version string join rejected, status 5 IP listed in ban.txt (ban/ngban/ispban) join rejected, status 6 Duplicate player GUID join rejected, status 8 Variant file edited, stored digest not fixed slot flagged +0x357C, mission entry aborted, event queued (self-enforcement) Variant file edited, digest recomputed (salt 0xA1252388 is public) passes — nothing cross-checks the file Patch outside the 15 loader regions (damage/armor math, variant parser, validators) passes — not hashed Replay/spoof the stock checksum + version pair passes — the pair is a pure function of shipped data, no nonce or secret Spoof the IP fields in 0x0A ban list bypassed Memory patch after join invisible — no re-validation during play

Runtime is peer-to-peer with no server authority: the net event table (0x0A– 0x31, FUN_00546C60) contains join/team/decal/mission/state handlers but no armor or damage message; the integrity checks are concentrated at join/load time, and each client simulates the shared world from its own local data.

docs.title: 11. Observed limitations
docs.text:
1. No secret, no challenge. The handshake is a self-report of a constant: the expected pair is a pure function of the shipped binary and mission data. A client can compute or replay it regardless of the code it actually runs. Without a host nonce (and a keyed response) the check cannot attest to the sender's binary.
  2. Tiny hashed surface. Only the 15 resource-loader functions and one mission archive entry are covered. The simulation, weapon/armor math, hit detection, damage application, the loadout validators, the variant parser, and the netcode itself are not.
  3. Weak mission-content contribution. FUN_00414A70 folds the mission digest to 8 bits (digest[0] ^ digest[8]), so the content side of the checksum has ≤ 256 effective values; the strength rests on the loader-code hash alone.
  4. Variant digest is local-only. The salt is a constant in the binary, the digest is stored in the file it protects, and the check compares the receiver's own file with itself. A client that recomputes the digest is not detected.
  5. Ban lists are IP-only and self-reported. The 0x0A IP fields come from the peer; the ban list is a local ban.txt, with no server-side or shared enforcement.
  6. Identity is self-reported. GUID1/GUID2 (the player identity used for the duplicate check) arrive in the message; a client can present arbitrary values.
  7. No runtime re-validation. Once in, nothing re-checks the peer; a patched process passes forever. The +0x357C flag is computed locally and is self-enforced.
  8. Divergence is undetected. Because variant data is not cross-checked, two clients can simulate different mechs and the game only notices when visible state conflicts.
  9. Reporting is opaque. Failures surface as Player_Reject <index> <code>; there is no user-facing "modified files" message (the variant flag becomes event code 1 in an internal queue with no dedicated string).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This is an educational and interoperability-focused study of the MechWarrior 4: Mercenaries binaries. It records the machine code as byte-exact, annotated MSVC6 assembly and provides the tooling to rebuild and verify the canonical images.

It is not the original source code and is not a game distribution.

docs.title: What is included
docs.text:
• Transcribed code (func_*.c) and in-.text data tables.
  • Byte-exact non-.text data runs (.rdata, .data, .rsrc, .txt2) and the metadata artifacts needed to assemble the images.

These are derived from the original game and are included so the default build is self-contained.

docs.title: What is not included
docs.text:
• No original MW4Mercs.exe or game DLLs.
  • No art, audio, maps, missions, localization data, or other standalone game assets.
  • No SafeDisc/DRM implementation.

The reference binaries are optional. They are not distributed here and are only needed for regeneration or byte-diff checks; verify them against reference/SHA256.txt.

docs.title: User responsibility
docs.text: You do not need to own the game to build the oracle from the committed sources and artifacts. If you supply reference binaries for regeneration or verification, you must own a legitimate copy of the game and comply with its license/EULA.

docs.text: Rights in the original MechWarrior 4: Mercenaries code and assets remain with their respective owners. docs.title: Verification
docs.text: The acceptance criterion is byte identity with the canonical reference, not a similarity score. The default build is reference-free: it uses the committed data sources and .bin artifacts. The hash gate is the reference-free acceptance check; the byte-diff checks are optional diagnostics that run when a reference binary is present.

docs.title: 1. Hash gate
docs.text:
nmake verify

tools/verify_hashes.py compares the built images to the canonical hashes in reference/SHA256.txt:

Binary SHA-256 MW4Mercs.exe deb0cb7f97e26c9db850d768900bdfb7648db7d10a090e7cdf6cecdc7686134f blade.dll d774c9fd2473e069c5c183333e07518392f2782b35582e2672a9479164652c6a GunDll.dll 1e441bc27cf7779d893dc59d2cf52b39c28dee17172f0ae08edd183e481b2410 MW4Stats.dll 61de52cb1606422181e03f87e1eeb944b705d69da1ab1e564a566d588ab814d5 ZlogLib.dll 03af8be5d047ba02076253009523461ab25922376e2af6a3db1d523df259b295 Language.dll 8cacab8c2eb11ba1829ca2e57920bd8e191be8c8178dbb7e00352e65ef80c1d6 MissionLang_MERCS.dll 280d422c13d428bc4b4b17d7809ace628b10927047c2f5e37aadeb337f0db1b3

This gate does not read the reference binaries.

docs.title: 2. Full-image byte diff (optional)
docs.text:
nmake exe
nmake dll-all MOD=gundll

When reference/MW4Mercs.exe or the module's reference DLL is present, the assembler compares the complete image to it with no masking. This is an additional diagnostic and catches:

  • function ordering and overlap errors,
  • missing or wrong inter-function padding,
  • section composition errors,
  • unresolved or mis-resolved relocations,
  • data-section placement errors.

If the reference file is absent, the diff is skipped and the build still succeeds.

A successful diff prints:

diff: byte-identical to reference (SHA-256 ...)

or, for a module:

== <module>: byte-identical to reference (no masking, reference-free build) ==

docs.title: 3. Per-function checks (optional)
docs.text:
nmake diff FUNC=0x00401000 OBJNAME=build\obj\func_00401000.obj
nmake nomask FUNC=0x00401000 OBJNAME=build\obj\func_00401000.obj

tools/diff.py slices the reference function's bytes from the binary and compares them to the compiled object's .text section. Four-byte relocation sites are masked because an unlinked object still contains placeholder values there.

tools/verify_nomask.py places the object at its reference VA, resolves every relocation from the symbol name and the committed src\<target>\artifacts\extern_addrs.csv table, and compares every byte. This catches misaligned or spurious relocation sites that the masked diff hides.

Both checks need the corresponding reference binary.

docs.title: Reproducibility notes
docs.text:
• The PE timestamp/checksum/Rich header are pinned by the committed pe_headers.bin artifact, not by the current clock.
  • The generated non-.text data sources and .bin artifacts are committed. The default build reads no reference content.
  • nmake data, nmake init, and nmake dll-init are the optional regeneration path; they read a reference binary to rebuild the committed data/artifacts.
  • The build is not run in GitHub Actions: the pinned MSVC6 toolchain is not available on hosted runners. Verification is a local Windows gate.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• The hash gate is keyed to the canonical hashes. A different source tree or toolchain will fail it.
  • The per-function diff uses reference/functions/*.csv for sizes. Functions missing from that inventory can be checked with an explicit SIZE=....
  • gundll intentionally has out-of-scope .text ranges; its coverage report uses reference/in_scope/gundll.txt. The full-image diff is still available when the reference DLL is present.

docs.text:
The four authoring/config EXEs shipped with MW4:Mercenaries. These are record + RE-documentation assets only — never oracle targets (reference assets only). Hashes in reference\SHA256.txt; Analyzed with Ghidra; the analysis projects and dumps are not part of this repository.

docs.text: File Producer Consumer Format Resource\Maps\*.mw4 MapCreator game #VBD v4 archive (map def → Tctd.exe output) Resource\MISSIONS\*.mw4 MW4Ed2 game #VBD v4 archive (multi-group directory; mission object + aspects + scripts) Resource\Missions\*.nfm / UserMissions\*.nfm NFMEditor (+ MW4Ed2 scenario dialogs) game server GameOS "info file" text servercycle.txt NFMEditor game server info-file rotation list (map=Name::Scenario) options.ini autoconfig (game startup autoconfig too) game INI with Graphics/Sound/Special options

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Common base: NFMEditor, MapCreator and autoconfig are thin MFC shells (dynamic MFC42) over the bundled GameOS framework; MW4Ed2 is the same but at ~10× the scale, embedding the full game runtime (blade/gundll/ DirectPlay/ABL/localization) — 11,388 functions.
  • Format of record: MW4Ed2's mission #VBD member layout is the deepest remaining open question (multi-group directory encoding — see the include/mw4/vbd.h follow-up note).
  • Cross-references: the game's own CLI/option surface (-noautoconfig, option table 0x0076C918) matches what autoconfig writes; these docs reference material for the oracle analysis only.

docs.title: autoconfig_MERCS.exe — GameOS AutoConfig / Driver-Diagnostics Tool (deep-dive)
docs.text: Reference record; not an oracle target. Analyzed with Ghidra; the analysis project and dumps are not part of this repository. No source tree, no byte-identity gate.

docs.title: 1. Binary facts
docs.text:
File reference\autoconfig_MERCS.exe Size 913,408 B (0xDF000) SHA-256 844058f3ba1ad4bd4cedd81028e3f8ed71260433fd00b0b39cc83902c62f5f5c Toolchain MSVC6, Linker 6.0, TimeDateStamp 2002-09-30 21:04:19Z Machine / Subsystem x86 (0x014C) / GUI (2) ImageBase / Entry 0x00400000 / 0x00542A6 Rich header XOR key 0x5C43216D, DanS @ 0x80 (MSVC6 tools) Functions 1,128 (Ghidra)

Sections (4 — no SafeDisc .txt2):

Section RVA VSize RawSize Notes .text 0x1000 0x5544E 0x56000 GameOS core + app shell .rdata 0x57000 0xED6E 0xF000 strings (huge D3D/DDERR/DIERR error tables), vtables .data 0x66000 0x76818 0x2000 mostly zero-init GameOS global state (~0x74818 BSS tail) .rsrc 0xDD000 0x18C8 0x2000 dialog resources

Imports (10 DLLs): MFC42 112 (dynamic MFC shell), MSVCRT 66, KERNEL32 84, USER32 63, GDI32 12, ADVAPI32 12, ole32 3, MSACM32 7, VERSION 3, WINMM 5 — the same import set family as NFMEditor (same FASA shell base).

docs.title: 2. Purpose
docs.text:
This is not a lightweight graphics-settings editor. It is the GameOS "AutoConfig" driver-diagnostics tool (version string 50.06.09.3002, build tag Version 1.1 11/2/2000):

  1. Probes the machine — processor details, PCI card info, DirectX version, audio/video codec install, modem/lobby providers (GetMachine Details, GetProcessorDetails, GetDirectXDetails, GetGameDetails, GetInstallAudioVideoCodecs, GetPCICardInfo).
  2. Runs the GameOS renderer/driver test suite — enumerates D3D devices, display modes, texture formats and caps, render states, gamma calibration, video memory (local/non-local/AGP), AGP miniport mode (viaagp1.sys detection, TURBO/NORMAL), and DirectSound devices — exactly the same driver probes the game's own startup autoconfig runs.
  3. Writes the results — the selected device/options into options.ini (§4), a VideoCard.txt driver report, and the game registry key Software\Microsoft\Microsoft Games\<game> (§5).
  4. Reports bugs — can submit a crash/report to the FASA "Raid" SQL database (DRIVER={SQL Server};SERVER=%s;...;APP=RAID4).

The tool is the standalone, interactive form of the game's built-in autoconfig — the same GameOS code paths that MW4Mercs' -noautoconfig switch skips.

docs.title: 3. Layout — .text regions
docs.text: Range Size Content 0x401000–0x404xxx ~20 KB App shell + the options.ini writer (FUN_00401b70) 0x405xxx–0x406xxx ~10 KB INI/section writer helpers (0x403a50, 0x404bd0, 0x4065c0, 0x4067d0) 0x40xxxx–0x44xxxx ~300 KB GameOS core — the same framework as the game EXE: config/CLI (FUN_00413c50 parses /gosconfig, /gosnovideo, /gosnosound), registry (FUN_0041c9b0), renderer state, texture manager, DirectSound mixer, input 0x45xxxx+ — VideoCard.txt reporter (FUN_00428a30), PCI-card detail (FUN_00441dc0), sound-device details (FUN_004201c0) 0x457000–0x465D6E — .rdata: the full D3D/DDERR/DIERR/DSERR error-string tables + render-state enums

docs.title: 4. options.ini — what AutoConfig writes
docs.text:
The writer (FUN_00401b70, thiscall on a config object) emits an INI with three sections and the game's option keys as name=value lines:

[Graphics Options]
VideoDriverIndex          DetailTexture    MultiTexture    LightMaps
Culturals                 Footsteps        MissionMusic     NoBlend
AntiAlias                 VertexLighting   SimpleLighting   MipBias
ShadowMode                screenwidth      screenheight     bitdepth
FancyWater                MovieTextures    MaxLights        Compositing
EffectLOD                 LoadRadius       AllowDecalTransfer
[Sound Options]
LowEndSound               Radius
[Special Commands]
KillGame

Plus the font keys fontsmall / fontmedium / fontlarge / fontlarge2 / fontlarge3 and server. Values are read from the config object's fields (+0x240, +0x340, +0x440, ... — per-option), converted to text via a 0x147-typed formatter, and written through the section writer helpers (0x4067d0 / 0x4065c0). screenwidth/screenheight/bitdepth are the display-mode selection; VideoDriverIndex picks the D3D device.

These keys are the same option names the MW4Mercs option table consumes (the game EXE's option table at 0x0076C918 + -noautoconfig interplay — cross-reference only).

docs.title: 5. Registry / file side effects
docs.text:
• Software\Microsoft\Microsoft Games\%s (0x45959C, written from FUN_0041c9b0) — the per-game config key; %s is the game/product name.
  • Software\Microsoft\Multimedia\Sound Mapper\ (0x45AD00) + \DirectSound\ Mixer Defaults / Device Presence — sound device selection.
  • Software\Microsoft\Windows Messaging Subsystem (0x45CEA8) and Config Manager\Enum\ (0x61AC0, hardware key DeviceDesc, HardWareKey, DriverDate, videoram from FUN_00441dc0) — PCI/device enumeration.
  • VideoCard.txt (0x45BD04, written by FUN_00428a30) — a driver report (driver file/version/date/size, video memory, renderer caps).
  • Screen.bmp (0x5D088) — screen-capture output (GameOS @Kscreen%04d.%s screenshot naming).

docs.title: 6. Per-card compatibility flags
docs.text:
.rdata holds the GameOS per-card workaround registry — the same compatibility knobs the game applies for broken drivers:

SceneRenderer, NoMultitexture, NoAlphaTest, NoStretchTexture, RenderEqualZ, BrokenAlphaTest, ForceSquareTextures, LimitTextureSize, Limit500VidTextures, AllowLowMemoryCard, DisableTextureDeletes, SlowDisplayModeChange, TextureOffset, LowEndCard.

These are the auto-selected renderer/tuning flags; AutoConfig tests the device and enables the appropriate ones before writing the option set.

docs.title: 9. Notes
docs.text:
• The tool shares its GameOS core with the game EXE and the other editor tools (identical CLI switches, registry paths, D3D error tables) — it is the best standalone reference for what the game's startup autoconfig does and which options.ini keys the game reads.
  • .data VSize (0x76818) is ~95% BSS — the GameOS renderer/sound/input global state, mirroring the game's own globals; no layout captured here.
  • No .txt2/SafeDisc section (unlike MW4Ed2).

docs.title: MapCreator.exe — bitmap → .mw4 map authoring tool (deep-dive)
docs.text: Reference record; not an oracle target. Analyzed with Ghidra; the analysis project and dumps are not part of this repository. No source tree, no byte-identity gate.

docs.title: 1. Binary facts
docs.text:
File reference\MapCreator.exe Size 528,384 B (0x81000) SHA-256 4f1a37548b352fd36e99a71aded94db13253f9ec84c6d350237b525f5936ea7d Toolchain MSVC6, Linker 6.0, TimeDateStamp 2002-11-26 20:47:03Z Machine / Subsystem x86 (0x014C) / GUI (2) ImageBase 0x00400000 Sections .text RVA 0x1000 VSize 0x68ABB · .rdata RVA 0x6A000 · .data RVA 0x7C000 VSize 0x78358 (raw 0x3000 — most of .data is zero-fill; the tool's literal strings live in the raw part at 0x47C000–0x47C9xx) · .rsrc RVA 0xF5000 Imports MFC42 (135), MSVCRT (76), KERNEL32 (85), USER32 (63), GDI32 (12), ADVAPI32 (12), ole32 (3), MSACM32 (7), VERSION (3), WINMM (5) Functions 1,556 (Ghidra)

Like NFMEditor, it bundles GameOS and must run from the game install root (Cannot find Language.dll in %s\assets\binaries or %s, this file is required, GameOS build version, Exit:DestroyTextureManager). It also links the Stuff:: engine classes (Stuff::FileStream, Stuff::TreeNodeOf) and a full image-decoding library (TIFF/GIF/TGA/PNG/BMP + zlib + libpng).

docs.title: 2. Purpose and pipeline
docs.text:
MapCreator converts a heightfield bitmap + textures into a playable map .mw4. The overall flow (from the writer/handlers):

bitmap (TIF/GIF/TGA/PNG)  ──>  heightfield (256..1024 wide × 256..2048 high,
                               multiple of 256, 24-bit for "interest data")
                                     │
            MapCreator writes (Content\ + Resource\ trees under the game root):
              Content\Maps\<name>                 map definition "info file"
              Content\Maps\<name>\<name>.build     build manifest
              Content\Maps\<name>\tctd.ini         Tctd input config
              Content\Maps\<name>\tctd.ini.bsp     Tctd BSP input config
              Content\textures\maps\...            copied/renamed textures
              Maps\<name>\<name>.instance          instance info
                                     │
            shell:  Tctd /f Content\Maps\<name>\tctd.ini
            shell:  Tctd /f Content\Maps\<name>\tctd.ini -bsp
                                     │
            Tctd.exe builds the final packed map:
              Resource\Maps\<name>.mw4             a #VBD archive (see §7)

Tctd.exe ("Terrain converter/compiler") is an external tool that must be present (Cannot Find Tctd.exe,Make sure this file exists and try again); MapCreator shells out to it with system(). Tctd is what produces the binary terrain/BSP data packed into the final .mw4. The tool then reports Map created successfully. Run Mission Editor to create a mission with this map (or There was an Error in Createing your map [sic] on failure).

docs.title: 3. Layout — .text regions
docs.text:
Range Content 0x401000–0x4072xx Tool UI + map pipeline (heightfield load/validate, texture pickers, map create/save, Tctd launch) 0x408xxx–0x44Exxx Bundled GameOS / Stuff:: engine (file system, textures, DirectX, DirectSound, image codecs) 0x45xxxx–0x465xxx GameOS config/profile + helpers 0x466Bxx+ Ordinal thunks (MFC/GameOS imports)

The Ghidra inventory names imports Ordinal_XXXX (jmp-thunk table at 0x466B80+). Key ordinal semantics seen in the map code: Ordinal_926/924/ 922 = path-combine string ops, Ordinal_858 = write/create, Ordinal_800 = close, Ordinal_540 = push a "file op" guard, Ordinal_5683 = strrchr, Ordinal_4277 = substring after last \, Ordinal_4129 = strrchr('.'), Ordinal_2818 = sprintf, Ordinal_941 = append to command line, Ordinal_860 = get app path, Ordinal_6334 = _ftol-family.

docs.title: 4. The map definition "info file" (Content\Maps\<name>)
docs.text:
The map definition is written with the same GameOS info-file format that NFMEditor uses (sections, key=value, case handling — see docs/editor_tools/nfmeditor.md §4). The map file's root carries a gamedata section (all keys below, written by FUN_004021b0 / FUN_004012b0):

Key Value grid <name>.erf — the grid/terrain source file cull nevercull class mechwarrior4::mwmap — the map class tag texturedata <name>.fgd tcffilename <name>.index.tcf waterlevel float (water plane height) watertexture path to water texture underwatertexture path to underwater texture waterdetailtexture path to water detail texture HudMap path to the HUD/minimap texture InputPath input bitmap path MapCenter two floats, e.g. "%.1f %.1f" (grid center; this+0x64 × 0x458280 scale const ×2) SmoothingPasses int (heightfield smoothing passes, this+0xbc) PolyCount int (target poly count, this+0xc0) HeightField heightfield file name DeltaY float (vertical scale, this+0xb8)

Texture/geometry files referenced by the definition: - <name>.fgd — the textured-terrain descriptor, - <name>.index.tcf — the texture-collection/flag file, - <name>.erf — the terrain grid source.

docs.title: 5. Heightfield input rules (from the validator at ~0x401480–0x401780)
docs.text:
Rule Message exists HeightField Does Not Exist / Bad Height Field width 256..1024 HeightField Width is too small, must be at least 256 / HeightField Width is too large, Cannot be larger than 1024 height 256..2048 HeightField Height is too small, must be at least 256 / HeightField Height is too large, must be at most 2048 both multiple of 256 HeightField has incorrect size, must be a multiple of 256 i.e. 256,512,768,1024... 24-bit when "Interest data" used HeightField must be 24-bit while using "Interest data"

File dialog filter: Bitmap Images (*.tif,*.gif,*.tga,*.png)|*.tif;*.gif;*.tga;*.png||. The image decoder handles TIFF (Tiff Error-*), GIF, TGA, PNG (libpng), BMP, JPEG (via ijl10.dll).

docs.title: 6. Texture rules
docs.text: Texture Constraint Terrain texture must exist, must be valid (Terrain Texture Does Not Exist / Bad Terrain Texture); size must equal the heightfield: For a Heightfield of %ix%i Terrain Texture should be %ix%i Detail texture Detail Texture Does Not Exist / Bad Detail Texture; Detail Texture MUST be 256x256 Water / water-detail / underwater must exist; all MUST be 256x256 (Water Texture Texture MUST be 256x256 [sic], etc.) Selection FGD Files (*.fgd)|*.fgd|| dialog for the FGD; textures written under Content\textures\maps\ with the %s\%s.Tga / %s\%c%c\%s_%c%c_0_0000.Tga naming pattern

docs.title: 7. The final map archive — Resource\Maps\<name>.mw4 is a #VBD
docs.text:
The shipped maps (e.g. carps01.mw4, 7–27 MB) are #VBD v4 archives — the container documented in include/mw4/vbd.h. Verified on carps01.mw4: sig #VBD, version 4, key1==key2==0x108, filetime, flags 1/1, archive path resource\maps\carps01.mw4 (25 chars incl. extension).

Two observations beyond vbd.h:

  • The directory is multi-group. After the header/path, the directory is organised as a sequence of blocks, each block = a path + its member entries: e.g. maps\carps01\carps01.instance, then entry rows textures\composttexture\arctic01_color_rock_active.bid, textures\composttexture\alpine01_color_rockfaceshale_active.bid, ... — one per map asset. entry_count=63 in the header is a capacity/count field, not the actual member count of every archive.
  • Members are compressed binary. The .instance/.bid members are binary, high-entropy (LZW-style, uncompressed_size > stored_size; the decompressor is the game's FUN_006FC220, see AGENTS.md "Compression codec — LZW"). data_off is relative to dir_file_offset and members are laid out contiguously (next.data_off == prev.data_off + prev.stored_size).

So MapCreator itself never writes a #VBD — it writes the info-file definition + textures and lets Tctd.exe produce the packed archive.

(The info-file parse/serialize library itself is the same GameOS family as NFMEditor's §4 map — the parser here is the MapCreator's bundled copy.)

docs.title: 9. Bundled engine / libraries
docs.text:
• GameOS: file system (Stuff::FileStream, memory-mapped files, Too many files, File '%s' is still open), texture manager (InitializeTextureManager called twice!, Exit:DestroyTextureManager, texture filter/format diagnostics), Direct3D/DirectDraw/DirectSound/DirectInput error tables, driver/registry dump (VideoCard.txt, Driver version, \Config\Platform), Language.dll loader, DirectPlay (DPERR_*), sound (acmStreamOpen, MSADPCM/PCM only).
  • Image codecs: TIFF ((Is Tiff)Invalid File, Tiff Error-Wrong Version), GIF, TGA (Only 256 color palletized, 24 or 32 bit TGA files supported), PNG (libpng — Not a PNG file, Incompatible libpng version), BMP ("..." is an invalid .BMP file), JPEG (ijl10). Plus zlib. The (Create Fade) / (MaskTo) / (MakeRGB) / (UnDifference) / (Deinterlace) strings are a generic image-processing helper library.
  • Stuff:: engine classes: Stuff::FileStream, Stuff::TreeNodeOf.
  • MAPI support (MAPISendMail, Bad MAPI32.DLL) and the same RAID/SQL connection string as NFMEditor (DRIVER={SQL Server};...).

docs.title: 11. Key data-structure take-aways
docs.text:
1. MapCreator writes an info-file map definition tagged class=mechwarrior4::mwmap (the gamedata section keys in §4) — the same GameOS key/value grammar as .nfm.
  2. The heavy lifting (binary terrain/BSP + final packing into the #VBD .mw4) is delegated to the external Tctd.exe; MapCreator only stages inputs and textures. The shipped Resource\Maps\*.mw4 are therefore Tctd's output, not MapCreator's.
  3. Heightfields are strictly bounded: 256..1024 wide, 256..2048 high, both a multiple of 256, 24-bit when "interest data" is enabled.
  4. Terrain texture must match the heightfield size; detail/water textures are fixed 256×256.
  5. The #VBD map archives use a multi-group directory (each asset group has its own path prefix) — a layout detail not captured in vbd.h, whose entry_count=63 field is not the member count. Worth a follow-up update to include/mw4/vbd.h.

docs.title: MW4Ed2.exe — Mission/Level Editor (deep-dive)
docs.text: Reference record; not an oracle target. Analyzed with Ghidra; the analysis project and dumps are not part of this repository. No source tree, no byte-identity gate.

docs.title: 1. Binary facts
docs.text:
File reference\MW4Ed2.exe Size 3,833,856 B (0x3A8000) SHA-256 7b19a1cbc18b2f4c16fd8fdeb9e44c2861c97464e8275e28817b28bbdae03b60 Toolchain MSVC6, Linker 6.0, TimeDateStamp 2002-11-26 23:53:19Z Machine / Subsystem x86 (0x014C) / GUI (2) ImageBase / Entry 0x00400000 / 0x00727C54 (in .text) Rich header XOR key 0xF2BFBE51, DanS @ 0x80 (MSVC6 tools, ProdId 0x000C/0x000B/0x000A/0x0013/0x0001 mixes) Functions 11,388 (Ghidra) — the largest of the four editor tools by ~10×

Sections (5 — note the SafeDisc .txt2, same as the game EXE):

Section RVA VSize RawSize Notes .text 0x1000 0x3393F2 0x33A000 game + editor + framework code .txt2 0x33B000 0x17C5 0x2000 SafeDisc leftover (out of scope) .rdata 0x33D000 0x4F8B4 0x50000 strings, vtables, IAT .data 0x38D000 0x1059C8 0xA000 initialized data + ~0x659C8 zero tail .rsrc 0x493000 0x101F8 0x11000 resources

Imports (import dir at RVA 0x38A3F0, 15 DLLs, ~736 functions): MFC42 356 (dynamic MFC — the editor shell), KERNEL32 107, MSVCRT 111, USER32 90, GDI32 28, ADVAPI32 12, MSACM32 7, ole32 5, WINMM 5, SHELL32 4, VERSION 3, COMCTL32 2, WSOCK32 2, plus the DRM imports (ARTPCLNT 1, CdaC14BA 3). The binary also names (LoadLibrary/delay-style references, not import-table) the full game runtime: blade.dll/bladed.dll (renderer wrapper + its debug build), gundll.dll (object library), dplayx.dll, dinput/ddraw/d3dim/ dsound, amstream/quartz/msacm/Ir50_32/ijl10 (Indeo/JPEG codecs), Language.dll/MissionLang_MERCS.dll/ScriptStrings_MERCS.dll (localization), machin16/32.dll, dbghelp/imagehlp, debug CRTs (msvcrtd/msvcirtd) alongside release — the tool was built against both runtime flavors.

docs.title: 2. Purpose
docs.text: MW4Ed2 is FASA's Mission Editor 2 — a full in-house mission/level editor that embeds the complete game runtime (renderer through blade, object code through gundll, DirectPlay, the ABL scripting VM, localization). It creates and edits the Resource\Missions\*.mw4 mission archives: pick a map (≈ \Games\*.mw4 browser), lay out spawns/units/lights/drop-zones/skies, bind ABL mission scripts and bot AI, and write the archive whose members are the serialized MechWarrior4::MWMission object graph plus per-aspect binary blobs. It is the companion to MapCreator (which builds the maps/mission terrain) — MW4Ed2 builds what runs on top of a map.

docs.title: 3. Architecture — a game framework with an editor shell
docs.text:
Two layers:

  • MFC editor shell (356 MFC42 imports): dialogs, toolbars, file dialogs, the \Games\*.mw4 map browser and Resource\Missions\*.nfm / Resource\UserMissions\*.nfm scenario dialogs. Thin compared to the framework below.
  • Bundled game framework (the bulk of .text): the same class/property system the MW4Mercs engine uses, driven headlessly:
  • Class registry — FUN_0046a280(size, "Class::Name", base, ...) registers serializable classes by name; FUN_006d3d80(name, ...) is a second registry flavor. Objects are identified in files by their class tag string (Adept::Mission, MechWarrior4::MWMission).
  • Property system — FUN_00469910(index, "Name", type, offset) + FUN_00469c60(list) register reflected, offset-addressed fields per class. This is the serialization contract (§5).
  • Allocator/factory — FUN_00449aa0(size) (calloc-like, returns 0 on failure); FUN_00449ab0(p) free.
  • GameOS framework (shared with the other editor tools + the game): file system finder (FUN_0043d7e0 set path / FUN_0043d850 next / FUN_0043d9b0), string table loader, the game console/message color helper (FUN_005a4bf0(0xbb7ff, ...) = blue "loading" text).
  • ABL scripting VM — FUN_005a6270(path, ...) compiles/loads an ABL script; mission and bot behavior is ABL (see §6).
  • Full runtime side-loading — the renderer (blade) and object library (gundll) DLLs are referenced by name, so the editor can actually run/render the level being edited.

docs.title: 4. The mission file format (Resource\Missions\*.mw4)
docs.text: Ground truth from the shipped coliseum.mw4 (58,948 B) and the sibling mission archives (0001.mw4, alpine.mw4, avalon01.mw4, ...).

docs.title: 4.1 Container — #VBD v4 (see include/mw4/vbd.h)
docs.text: Header (43 bytes + path): #VBD (4) · version 4 (4) · count=63 (4) · dir_off (4) · keys (4) · filetime (8) · flags1=0x1A (4) · flags2=0x1A (4) · reserved (6) · path-len (1) · path (resource\missions\coliseum.mw4, 30 chars). The count=63 is a capacity, not the member count.

docs.title: 4.2 Directory — multi-group rows
docs.text:
The directory is a sequence of fixed-prefix rows grouped by a shared FILETIME:

filetime (8)  u32  u32  u32  u16 index  u8 name-len  name[..]

All rows in a group carry the same filetime; consecutive groups differ (a group = one filetime run, e.g. one save session). Member names observed for coliseum:

missions\coliseum\coliseum.instance        (index 1)
missions\coliseum\coliseum.data{Element}
missions\coliseum\coliseum.data{GameModel}
missions\coliseum\coliseum.data
missions\coliseum\coliseum.lights
missions\coliseum\coliseumnight.lights
missions\coliseum\DropZones\DropTeam2.contents
missions\coliseum\DropZones\SecondaryLanceStart.contents
missions\coliseum\skies\colsm01_sky\colsm01_sky.erf
missions\coliseum\mission.bounds
missions\coliseum\coliseumgraph.data
missions\coliseum\scripts\Coliseum.abl
missions\coliseum\scripts\Coliseum_SinglePlayer.abl
missions\coliseum\scripts\Coliseum_Campaign.abl
missions\coliseum\scripts\player.abl
... (per-game-type script variants)

Member semantics: .instance (the serialized mission object, see §4.3), .data{...} aspect sub-blobs, .lights/...night.lights (light lists), DropZones\*.contents (spawn/drop-zone sets), skies\<map>_sky\*.erf (environment resource), mission.bounds (bounds), <name>graph.data (nav/unit graph), scripts\*.abl (mission scripts per game type).

docs.title: 4.3 First member — the serialized mission object
docs.text:
The first member's content begins directly with the map reference as a NUL-terminated path, followed by binary object data:

"resource\maps\colsm01.mw4"   \0  <binary mission object serialization...>

i.e. the mission archive is an object graph whose first field is the backing map. The exact directory → data-offset encoding is not fully resolved (multiple groups, variable-length rows; maps decode cleanly at data_off = prev.data_off + prev.stored_size relative to dir_off, but the mission archives interleave group headers — see the #VBD follow-up note in include/mw4/vbd.h).

docs.title: 5.1 Class registration
docs.text:
• Adept::Mission — registered by FUN_00462610 (3,144 B) via FUN_0046a280(0x1E6, "Adept::Mission", base, factory, ...) → class size 0x1E6 (486 bytes). This is the mission environment base class.
  • MechWarrior4::MWMission — registered by FUN_00585f60 via FUN_0046a280(0x420, "MechWarrior4::MWMission", ...) → class size 0x420 (1056 bytes); also constructs the StartMusicStatus and TransMusicStatus helper objects. This is the MW4 concrete mission subclass (the .instance member's top-level type).
  • Mission — registered by FUN_006d3d80("Mission", ...).

docs.title: 5.2 Adept::Mission property table (the serialized environment)
docs.text:
FUN_00462610 registers 55 reflected properties (index, name, type-code, offset-in-class). Type codes seen: 1=int, 2=float, 0xE=bool, 0x10=color/vector4, 0x231=string/resource. docs.title: 6. ABL scripting integration
docs.text:
Mission behavior is bound through ABL scripts stored as archive members (scripts\*.abl), one set per game type (Stock_MissionPlay, Campaign, SinglePlayer, ...), plus shared library scripts:

  • content\ablscripts\miscfuncs.abl — loaded by FUN_00586090 (the ABL library bootstrap; blue "loading" console message, then FUN_005a6270(path, ...) — the ABL compile/load entry).
  • Content\ABLScripts\StockScripts\Stock_MissionPlay.abl — referenced by the mission object (FUN_00586a90's cluster) as the default stock mission script.
  • Content\ABLScripts\Bots\UberBot.abl — the default bot AI script, loaded by the bot subsystem (FUN_00616430, FUN_00616f80, FUN_00618d00, FUN_0061b540 — a 4-site bot-script family in the 0x61xxxx region).
  • scriptName (0x00753954) — the per-mission script-name property binding (referenced from the 0x569xxx mission region).

docs.title: 9. Notes / follow-ups
docs.text:
• #VBD directory encoding: the mission archives' multi-group directory (shared-filetime row runs, 23-byte prefix) does not match the map archives' single-group layout captured in include/mw4/vbd.h. Worth a dedicated decode pass of a mission archive's directory + data-offset rule.
  • Runtime integration: the editor can load blade/gundll and run the real renderer — the deepest value here is the format of the serialized MechWarrior4::MWMission object graph, which the game itself loads from the same Resource\Missions\*.mw4 files (and which MW4Ed2 writes).
  • Scale: 11,388 functions across a ~3.3 MB .text; this doc maps the mission-format surface and framework seams, not every editor dialog.

docs.title: NFMEditor.exe — .NFM Multiplayer/Server Config Editor (deep-dive)
docs.text: Reference record; not an oracle target. Analyzed with Ghidra; the analysis project and dumps are not part of this repository. No source tree, no byte-identity gate.

docs.title: 1. Binary facts
docs.text:
File reference\NFMEditor.exe Size 471,040 B (0x73000) SHA-256 173db0b5f7c7000febf86e7c21519c24f8e11cdab41730d049a1fd22aaf3aa21 Toolchain MSVC6, Linker 6.0, TimeDateStamp 2003-02-15 19:57:40Z Machine / Subsystem x86 (0x014C) / GUI (2) ImageBase 0x00400000 Sections .text RVA 0x1000 VSize 0x5CFDE · .rdata RVA 0x5E000 · .data RVA 0x6E000 VSize 0x775B0 · .rsrc RVA 0xE6000 Entry 0x0045BE5F Imports MFC42 (138), MSVCRT (66), KERNEL32 (84), USER32 (63), GDI32 (12), ADVAPI32 (12), ole32 (3), MSACM32 (7), VERSION (3), WINMM (5) Rich header XOR key 0x72BAA77B, DanS @ 0x80 (Linker 6.00 SP6 + C7 toolset) Functions 1,129 (Ghidra)

MFC42 is imported dynamically (no static MFC in .text), unlike the game EXE. The tool must run from the game install root — it loads GameOS resources and Language.dll from assets\binaries\, and reads/writes resource\Missions\*.nfm / resource\UserMissions\*.nfm.

docs.title: 2. Purpose
docs.text:
NFMEditor edits the .nfm "network/multiplayer mission" files that define a map's multiplayer rulesets and scenarios (see docs/editor_tools/README.md for the file's place in the game data set). Each map in resource\Missions\ / resource\UserMissions\ has one .nfm describing:

  • [info] — author / blurb / link / long display name,
  • [ruleset] — the list of game-type rules that may be launched on the map, each rule = a type=$(<GameType>) macro entry + optional team / alignment,
  • [scenarios] — named scenario blocks (Name={ ... }), each with a [server] sub-section of per-scenario settings (game type, teams, kill/respawn limits, night/weather/radar, tonnage/C-Bill caps, game length, script name) and optional team_N/bot_N sub-blocks for per-team and per-bot constraints.

It also edits the Server Cycle List (servercycle.txt, via -cycle <file>): a rotation of map=Name.nfm::ScenarioName entries the game server walks to cycle maps.

The .nfm/servercycle.txt text format is GameOS's generic "info file" parser (a C-preprocessor-like key/value grammar) — see §4.

docs.title: 3. Layout — .text regions
docs.text:
Range Size Content 0x401000–0x4072xx ~25 KB Editor app code (dialog, .nfm load/save, cycle list) 0x408xxx–0x44Exxx ~290 KB Bundled GameOS framework (same engine code as MW4Mercs.exe) 0x44F000–0x458xxx ~40 KB The "info file" parser/serializer library (pure, reusable) 0x459000–0x45BE00 ~12 KB MFC glue + GameOS helpers + Ordinal thunks (0x45BBxx–0x45BExx) 0x45EA00+ — Class vtables in .rdata (PTR_LAB_0045ea00 = app vtable)

The Ghidra inventory names most MFC imports by Ordinal_XXXX (jmp-thunk table at 0x45BB80+); e.g. Ordinal_2864 = the frame/app singleton accessor, Ordinal_6907 = list-control "set item text", Ordinal_3996 = list-control "insert column", Ordinal_3302 = list-control "get item text", Ordinal_2642 = MFC "invalidate" family, Ordinal_6199 = string lowercase, Ordinal_3998 = list "insert item".

docs.title: 4. The "info file" format (GameOS generic key/value text)
docs.text: .nfm, servercycle.txt, Content\GameTypes.h (the include), and the resource\missions\*.txt scenario-text files are all read by one parser family. Ground truth: the shipped files (see §5/§6) plus the parser below.

docs.title: 4.1 Grammar
docs.text:
Read line by line (\r\n or \n), 512-byte line buffer, 0x200 max per line:

  • Comments: // to end of line; /* ... */ block (multi-line; error "There is a missing */ in %s" on EOF). /* */ is stripped inline.
  • Line-continuation/escape: a line beginning with @ has the @ removed (used to force literal interpretation / preserve case on an otherwise lowercased line). Lines that do not start with @ are lowercased (_strlwr) unless !preservecase=true is in effect.
  • Whitespace: leading/trailing spaces and tabs on a line are trimmed; keys are right-trimmed.
  • [SectionName] — section header (name trimmed). A ]-less header is rejected (incomplete).
  • key=value — key/value pair in the current section. Keys may repeat (all occurrences are kept; lookups return the first, case-insensitive).
  • Name={ — a block: Name becomes a key whose value is a nested section list. Contents are parsed recursively until a lone } line closes the block. Serializer re-emits Name={ + nested sections + }. A missing } at EOF is an error ("There is a missing } in %s").
  • !directive — control directives (see 4.2).
  • #define name value — C-preprocessor-style macro definition (this is how Content\GameTypes.h works).
  • $(name) — macro reference, expanded recursively at parse time (the $(StockBattle) in the shipped files becomes 0). Any key=value line whose value contains $( is macro-expanded. Recursive expansion is cycle-guarded.
  • Bare lines — a line with no = and no [ creates a key with an empty value (harmless).

Macros are resolved from the macro table (name → value). #define lines add to it; unknown $(...) references resolve to the empty string.

docs.title: 4.2 Directives (!...)
docs.text: Directive Effect !include=<path> Parse <path> as another info file into the same tree; relative paths resolve against the including file's directory. Quoted paths allowed. Include files are deduped via an include cache (a file is parsed once). !concatenate=true\|yes\|1 Toggle concatenation mode (parser flag). !preservecase=true\|yes\|1 Toggle case preservation (default: keys/values lowercased). The shipped .nfm files set !preservecase=true. !<name>=<value> Define a custom macro/directive name → value.

docs.title: 4.3 In-memory tree
docs.text:
• Root/tree object: +0x00 first-section, +0x05 concatenate flag, +0x06 preservecase flag, +0x0c include list, +0x44 sorted section list (doubly linked, head at +0x44), +0x48 count, +0x4c parser context. Created by FUN_00451390, freed by FUN_00451510.
  • Section node (0x20 B, FUN_004524b0): +0x00 vtable, +0x04 parent, +0x14 name, +0x18 key list. Sections are kept sorted by name.
  • Key node (0x1C B, FUN_00453c40): +0x00 vtable, +0x04 owning section, +0x14 key name, +0x18 value string (or block). Every parse creates a new node (duplicate keys retained); FUN_00453b50 returns the first case-insensitive match.
  • Block contents are a nested section list hung off the block key (assembled by FUN_00454f20, serialized by FUN_00451b40).
