docs.title: 5. The .nfm format spec
docs.text: Ground truth = the 21 shipped files (resource\MISSIONS\*.nfm) + the editor's reader (FUN_00404f00) + writer (FUN_004060b0).

docs.title: 5.1 Top-level layout
docs.text:
!include=Content\GameTypes.h
!preservecase=true

[info]
author=...
info=...            (e.g. "Standard Mission")
link=...            (e.g. www.microsoft.com/games/mechwarrior4)
longname=...        (display name, e.g. "Alpine")

[ruleset]
type=$(StockBattle)         <- one line per allowed rule
type=$(StockTeamBattle)
team=8                      <- optional per-rule team count
alignment=6                 <- optional per-rule alignment

[scenarios]
ScenarioName={
[server]
    ruleset=$(StockDestruction)
    name=...                (optional)
    teamAllowed=0|1
    teamcount=<0..8>
    scenariotext=resource\missions\<file>.txt   (optional)
    ... more optional keys (5.3) ...
    team_0={ teamdata{ ... } }   (optional, see 5.4)
    bot_0={ botdata{ ... } }     (optional, see 5.5)
}

The shipped files use a tab to indent the [server] block's keys (the parser trims whitespace, so indentation is cosmetic).

docs.title: 5.2 Game-type macros (Content\GameTypes.h)
docs.text:
!include=Content\GameTypes.h is a preprocessor file, not a tree section: #define lines feed the macro table. Values:

Macro Value Macro Value $(StockBattle) 0 $(CustomBattle) 6 $(StockTeamBattle) 1 $(CustomTeamBattle) 7 $(StockDestruction) 2 $(CustomDestruction) 8 $(StockTeamDestruction) 3 $(CustomTeamDestruction) 9 $(StockMissionPlay) 4 $(CustomMissionPlay) 10 $(StockCampaign) 5 $(CustomCampaign) 11 $(CustomUndefined) 12 $(SinglePlayer) 13

GameTypeCount = CustomUndefined + 1 = 13 (the editor's per-type arrays are sized 13; index 13/SinglePlayer is a separate flag). Note the editor's display strings are the $(...) forms — the shipped defianceholds.nfm uses ruleset=$(StockMissionPlay) inside [server], which resolves to 4.

docs.title: 5.3 [server] keys, types and validation ranges (from the editor)
docs.text:
Key Type Range / values Written if ruleset int 0..12 (game-type index) always name string — always (map name) teamAllowed int 0 or 1 always teamcount int 1..8 (if teamAllowed); else forced 0/0 always scenariotext string path (e.g. resource\missions\des.txt) non-empty killLimit int 0 or 1 non-empty killLimitNumber int 1..99 (default 10) killLimit==1 respawnLimit int 0 or 1 non-empty respawnWaveNumber int 1..9 (default 1) respawnLimit==1 isNight int 0 or 1 non-empty weather int 0 or 1 non-empty radarmode int 0..2 always (0 default) onlyStockMech int 0 or 1 non-empty maximumtonnage int 25..100 non-empty maximumCBills int 2,000,000..34,999,999 non-empty gameLength int 1..120 (minutes) non-empty scriptName string custom script name non-empty

(The [server] keys are case-insensitive — the shipped files mix teamAllowed and teamcount casing; the writer emits teamcount lower-case.)

docs.title: 5.4 team_N block (teamdata sub-key)
docs.text:
Written per team index N while teamAllowed==1:

team_0={
teamdata{
maximumTonnage=25..100
minimumTonnage=25..100
maximumTotalTonnage=100..1600
maximumCBills=2000000..35000000
maximumTotalCBills=2000000..500000000
maxPlayersOnTeam=1..16
skin=<single char '0'-'9' or 'a'-'z'>
alignment=0..7
}
}

Each field is emitted only when set (a non-default value). Constraint checked: max ≥ min (else both invalidated).

docs.title: 5.5 bot_N block (botdata sub-key)
docs.text:
bot_0={
botdata{
botCount=1..14
team=<1..teamcount>        (only meaningful when teamAllowed==1)
maximumTonnage=25..100
minimumTonnage=25..100
maximumLevel=0..9
minimumLevel=0..9
}
}

docs.title: 5.6 [ruleset] details
docs.text: Repeated type=$(...) entries are the mechanism for a multi-rule map: each type= line is one allowed game type. Per-rule optional keys follow their type line: team=<1..8> (team count) and alignment=<0..6>. The stock alpine.nfm declares two rule groups (destruction + team-destruction, and battle + team-battle). The editor's per-type arrays (+0x4e8 flags, +0x554 team count, +0x588 alignment) mirror these. If the single-player flag is set, the writer emits a type=$(SinglePlayer) line in [ruleset].

docs.title: 5.7 Round-trip behavior
docs.text:
• Load (FUN_00404f00): parse <dir>\<map>.nfm, populate ruleset flags + scenario list + per-scenario server/team/bot rows; out-of-range values are clamped or dropped (defaults shown above).
  • Save (FUN_004060b0): rebuild the tree from the UI and serialize. Only non-default fields are written (except the always-written keys). The output is normalized: !include / !preservecase first, then [info], [ruleset], [scenarios]. The original file's own formatting/comment/order is not preserved (parse→modify→re-serialize).

docs.title: 6. The Server Cycle List (servercycle.txt)
docs.text:
• CLI: NFMEditor.exe -cycle <file> (also -cycle <file> with a trailing space). FUN_00401210 validates the argument ("INVALID PARAMETER - No parameter", "INVALID PARAMETER - No space after"); default file is servercycle.txt (FUN_004012c0, InitInstance).
  • Format (ground truth: the shipped ServerCycle.txt):
[cycle]
map=Shoreline.nfm::Shoreline3
map=Alpine.nfm::Alpine4
...

Each entry: map=<mapfile>::<ScenarioName> (scenario = the [scenarios] block name in the map's .nfm). The editor list shows two columns (map name, scenario/game-type) joined with ::. - Save: FUN_00402720 (invoked from the OnClose handler 0x00402E80, which prompts "Do you want to save the Server Cycle List?"). On exit with an empty list: "The current Server Cycle List is empty. ... will stay at its last saved state.". Success message: "Server Cycle List Saved.". - Row population from an .nfm is FUN_004023a0 (reads a scenario's [server] ruleset/teamAllowed/teamcount into one list row).

docs.title: 7. Editor UI structure (main dialog object offsets)
docs.text:
The main window object (thiscall param_1 throughout the handlers) layout:

Offset Control / field +0x20 / +0x24 parent handles (frame access via Ordinal_2864) +0x2c0 Server-cycle list control (columns: map, scenario) +0x340 Missions/UserMissions folder combo (0=resource\Missions\, 1=resource\UserMissions\) +0x380 Map listbox (populated from *.nfm by FUN_00401e00) +0x3c0 Rules list (18 columns, see below) +0x180 Bot list (7 columns) +0x400 longname edit +0x480 info edit +0x3a8 "has current file" flag +0x4dc app icon (ID 0x80) +0x4e8 13 × game-type enabled flag (one per GameTypeCount) +0x51c 13 × per-type custom script-name list head +0x554 13 × per-type team count (default 8) +0x588 13 × per-type alignment (default 6) +0x550 SinglePlayer flag (game-type index 13)

List columns (from FUN_00404b60):

  • Rules (+0x3c0, 18): Rule Name, Rule Set, Scenario Name, Team Allowed, Team Count, Scenario Text File Name, Kill Limit Allowed, Kill Limit Count, # of Waves Allowed, # of Waves Count, Night, Weather, Radar Mode, Stock 'Mechs Only, Max Tonnage, Max C-Bills, Game Length, Custom Script Name.
  • Teams (+0x380, 9): Team #, Max Tonnage, Min Tonnage, Max Total Tonnage, Max C-Bills, Max Total C-Bills, Max # of Players, Skin, Alignment.
  • Bots (+0x180, 7): Rule #, # of Bots, Team #, Max Tonnage, Min Tonnage, Max AI Level, Min AI Level.

Handlers: FUN_00404b60 = New/Open (sets columns, default file new.nfm or loads current via FUN_00404f00); FUN_00404f00 = load; FUN_004060b0 = save; FUN_00406ee0/00406fe0 = populate team/bot lists; FUN_00406eb0/00406fb0 = per-scenario team/bot data accessors; FUN_00407120/00407160 = ruleset helpers; 0x00402E80 = OnClose (cycle-list save prompt).

docs.title: 8. Bundled GameOS framework (0x408xxx–0x44Exxx)
docs.text:
The tool links a large slice of the GameOS engine (the same framework the game EXE uses), which is why it must run from the game root:

  • DirectSound init/caps dump (FUN_0041a0b0, 16.7 KB — the big SECONDARYMONO/SECONDARYSTEREO/MaxHwMixing*/FreeHw3D* report builder over the DAT_00470810 caps table), GameOS memory manager (heap tags DAT_004e4a38/004e4b48, "GameOS_Memory*", "GameOS Parent Heap"), file/mapped-file I/O (CreateFileMappingA, UnmapViewOfFile),
  • Direct3D/DirectDraw/DirectInput/DirectPlay wrapper error tables (D3DERR_, DDERR_, DIERR_, DPERR_), texture codecs (BMP/TGA/JPG loading, mipmap rules — the "Only power of 2..." diagnostics), registry helpers (\Config\Platform, Config Manager\Enum), AGP miniport detection,
  • Language.dll / blade.dll / gundll.dll / dbghelp.dll / dsetup.dll / ijl10.dll loader strings, GameOS.vxd, MAPI (MAPISendMail), a SQL connection string (DRIVER={SQL Server};...), VideoCard.txt dump.

This is the same subsystem family as the game EXE's bundled engine code; the .nfm reader/writer and the info-file library (§4) are the parts unique to this tool's workflow (the game EXE reads .nfm with its own copy of the same info parser — see src\mw4mercs).

docs.title: 10. Key data-structure take-aways
docs.text:
1. .nfm and servercycle.txt share one grammar: the GameOS info file format (sections, key=value, Name={ blocks, #define/! directives, $(macro) expansion, ////* */ comments).
  2. The format is case-insensitive by default; .nfm files opt out with !preservecase=true. Keys are lowercased on read otherwise.
  3. Duplicate keys are meaningful — a map's [ruleset] is a list of repeated type= lines; the parser retains every occurrence and readers take the first match.
  4. Game types are a 13-entry enum (0..12, 13 = SinglePlayer) defined by Content\GameTypes.h; the editor's state arrays are sized exactly 13.
  5. The writer normalizes output and only emits non-default optional fields — a hand-edited .nfm's formatting/comments are not preserved on save.

docs.title: Subsystem Documentation
docs.text:
Each subsystem has its own page: what it is responsible for, how the main path works, and its key entry points. The exhaustive per-VA tables live in the per-binary indexes; this overview and the subsystem pages link to them instead of repeating them.

Shared VAs are described once in shared.md. Boundary calls are in ../SUBSYSTEM_SEAMS.md.

docs.title: EXE subsystems
docs.text: Subsystem VAs What it covers Render 2708 Owns the MidLevelRenderer (MLR) scene pipeline and the D3D7 immediate-mode device boundary. It turns game state into sorted draw records, evaluates animation and lighting, streams terrain and textures, and hands final primitives to the device and present paths. Runtime 2626 Engine/runtime services: memory, reference counting, threads and locks, object lifetime, and virtual/command dispatch. Gameplay 2525 Simulation state and rules: mechs, movers, pilots, missions, objectives, teams, sensors, vehicles, and the collision and geometry queries they use. AI 1308 AI decision layer, ABL script runtime, navigation, targeting, squad control, and AI combat decisions. Database 691 Object/container model: binary-search trees, linked lists, iterators, hash tables, object tables, and database wrappers. UI 672 gosScript-driven 2D UI: HUD, menus, dialogs, cursor, and screen state. Network 382 Multiplayer transport, lobby/session state, GameSpy discovery, and ZoneMatch matchmaking. Archive 285 #VBD archives, streams, file I/O, and path handling. Platform 256 Win32/COM/DLL/registry glue, DirectDraw/D3D wrappers, import thunks, and the SafeDisc wrapper. Log 192 Logging, assertions, error reporting, and diagnostic output. Combat 141 In-mission weapon fire, launch/guidance, hit resolution, and damage application. C Runtime 21 C/C++ runtime helpers: strings, memory primitives, formatting, and math. Config 13 options.ini/config-file framework, option registry, and persistence. Input 11 Keyboard/mouse/joystick state and command bindings. Audio 8 Sound, music, and audio-device delivery. Crypto 6 MD5, hashing, and base64 helpers. Codec 2 LZW compression/decompression and related byte codecs.

docs.text:
Binary: MW4Mercs.exe | Classified VAs: 2708 | Exhaustive index: MW4Mercs.exe

Owns the MidLevelRenderer (MLR) scene pipeline and the D3D7 immediate-mode device boundary. It turns game state into sorted draw records, evaluates animation and lighting, streams terrain and textures, and hands final primitives to the device and present paths.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• How it works
  • Key entry points
  • Details
  • Inventory
  • Related

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The frame path starts at 0x00496280, which walks the active scene nodes and updates their render records. Camera and visibility code at 0x004C35B0 and 0x004C40E0 builds the view/frustum used by the traversal.

Geometry families under mesh and vertex build buffers and transforms. The animation detail evaluates curves and feeds node transforms; lighting selects light slots and light maps; terrain streams terrain nodes; texture decodes, caches, and uploads surfaces.

draw sorts and clips records and dispatches through the drawable table. device wraps the D3D7-IM calls at 0x00713A70-0x00713C80; present and display handle backbuffer and resolution changes; 2d and font draw screen-space clouds, sprites, and glyphs.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
UI code clusters at 0x00690000-0x0069FFFF, 0x006F0000-0x006F8FFF, and 0x00740000-0x0074FFFF. The screens and controls are data-driven gosScript objects; the C++ side manages screen state, control lists, and event dispatch.

Input events feed command state, and the render 2D/font details draw the result. A representative helper is 0x006F0770, which drives UI callbacks and conditional screen updates.

Rule: every VA appears under exactly one subsystem/detail section. role is core (system implementation), shared (used by multiple systems), boundary (called by the system but implemented elsewhere), data (non-code section or table), or unknown. confidence/reason record the evidence used.

Regenerated by tools/gen_master_index.py. See the subsystem overview and the seam summary.
